title: TimeProofs Action Types Registry
description: Initial documentation-oriented registry for future TimeProofs Action File v1 action types and proof-level guidance. This file does not enforce runtime validation yet.
schema_note: This registry is not a validation schema for Action Files. The future .action.json schema will be defined separately.
privacy_rules: Do not send sensitive action content to TimeProofs by default.
Use fingerprints for prompts, outputs, documents, API responses, or message bodies where possible.
Keep customer data and business content in customer-owned systems.
Use synthetic or redacted data in examples.

crm.lead_created.label: CRM lead created
crm.lead_created.description: An AI workflow creates or attempts to create a lead in a CRM.
crm.lead_created.notes: A target CRM reference improves traceability but does not prove lead quality, consent, legality, or CRM content correctness.

crm.record_updated.label: CRM record updated
crm.record_updated.description: An AI workflow updates or attempts to update a CRM record.
crm.record_updated.notes: The Action File can record that an update reference exists; it does not prove that the update was correct or authorized.

support.ticket_created.label: Support ticket created
support.ticket_created.description: An AI workflow creates or attempts to create a support ticket.
support.ticket_created.notes: The ticket reference helps reconstruct the action, but TimeProofs does not verify ticket content or support decisions.

email.drafted.label: Email drafted
email.drafted.description: An AI workflow drafts or prepares an email without confirming that it was sent.
email.drafted.notes: A drafted email does not prove that the email was sent, received, opened, lawful, or correct. Use fingerprints for subject/body content when possible.

email.sent.label: Email sent
email.sent.description: An AI workflow sends or attempts to send an email.
email.sent.notes: Use fingerprints for subject/body content when possible. Do not include recipient personal data in public examples.

document.generated.label: Document generated
document.generated.description: An AI workflow generates or attempts to generate a document.
document.generated.notes: Prefer a document fingerprint or storage reference instead of raw document content.

file.delivered.label: File delivered
file.delivered.description: An AI workflow or automation delivers a file to a target system, recipient, or storage location.
file.delivered.notes: Delivery reference does not prove that the recipient opened, accepted, or understood the file.

decision.recorded.label: Decision recorded
decision.recorded.description: An AI-assisted decision, recommendation, or decision-related event is recorded.
decision.recorded.notes: This action type is sensitive. Do not claim that TimeProofs proves the decision was correct, fair, lawful, or compliant.

request.classified.label: Request classified
request.classified.description: An AI workflow classifies an incoming request, ticket, message, document, or case.
request.classified.notes: A classification record does not prove that the classification is accurate or unbiased.
